design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (setaside_property_charges_and_repairs, env_0064).

0. DRAW: prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,5,6,6] (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1). Taken: setaside_ext_returned_flood_premium (root) 6, setaside_ext_returned_hazard_premium 6, setaside_ext_reserve_hazard_projection 6, setaside_ext_reserve_flood_projection 5.

1. SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied by task 0: setaside_ext_reserve_tax_projection / update_reserve_tax_b755da65 and setaside_ext_returned_tax_refund / return_tax_refund_0b9f20b8 (tax only). Claimed here, all new: the two insurance premium projections (update_reserve_hazard_5ea539e7, update_reserve_flood_ec384f8d, agent) and the two returned insurance premiums (return_hazard_premium_b6a621c2, return_flood_premium_57ae44ac, user). Last task: after it every extended policy is claimed exactly once. Charter-wide principle shared with task 0: a refund waits on the figures on file of its own kind of charge (tax for a tax refund; both insurance premiums for an insurance refund, because both enter its insurance part and month of charges), and reads the other kind as it stands; the flood refund additionally waits on the hazard refund because the two share the reserve balance and room.

2. DESIGN THESIS (revision 2 world). Caller Ellen Hargrove, executor and confirmed successor of Walter Hargrove (died 2026-06-20). Before his death Walter himself replaced both insurance policies on the occupied house: the HO3 policy (term from 2026-03-01, 4212.00) by another HO3 policy from 2026-06-01 (5640.00 in two installments), and the NFIP policy (term from 2026-04-15, 1750.00) by a private flood policy with higher limits from 2026-06-15 (2890.00 in two installments). Both current terms were therefore written at occupied / primary-residence rates and will renew (2027-06-01, 2027-06-15) on a house nobody lives in. Surface goal: pay the cancelled NFIP policy's refund (check 1415.89, deposited in the estate account) back into the Summit reserve. Scored core: the kept amount of the returned flood premium (1406.46). Hidden prerequisites: (a) the hazard premium on file (4212.00) and (b) the flood premium on file (1750.00) were set from the terms now withdrawn and never reviewed against the replacement bills received 2026-04-20 / 2026-05-01 -> both projections must be posted first (6178.40, 3164.55); (c) the estate also received the old homeowners carrier's return premium (2808.00, July) and the reserve's payment of that withdrawn hazard term carries no refund credit -> the returned hazard premium must be credited first (2793.61), which raises the balance the flood room is netted against. Tree: root -> {flood review, hazard review, hazard refund}; hazard refund -> {hazard review, flood review}.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD (five edges, all value_input; 3 prerequisite problems -> floor 2 met).
 E1 flood refund -> flood projection. gate flood_on_file, ACTION: "A returned flood premium's kept amount is not settled until the annual flood premium on file has been reviewed against every flood insurance bill received since it was last set." fallback: the review leaves only a changed number; the reserve carries no review date or bill link. Unresolved: annual_flood_premium 1750.00 (bill of the withdrawn NFIP term), replacement installment bills received 2026-05-01. Skip effect: hazard credit 2498.92, flood credit 1200.17 instead of 2793.61 / 1406.46.
 E2 flood refund -> hazard projection. gate haz_on_file, ACTION: "A returned flood premium's kept amount is not settled until the annual hazard premium on file has been reviewed against every hazard insurance bill received since it was last set." Unresolved: annual_hazard_premium 4212.00, replacement bills received 2026-04-20. Skip: 2383.95 / 1119.69.
 E3 flood refund -> hazard refund. gate reserve_balance, STATE: "The kept amount of a returned flood premium is fixed only after the reserve's payment of the latest withdrawn hazard insurance term carries a refund credit." (revision 2: "every" -> "the latest", matching the hazard rule's own selection of the withdrawn hazard bill with the latest due date, so the gate is always satisfiable by that rule's write.) Record-visible: a refund credit whose source_txn_ref is the payment of that bill; exactly one write of the difficulty books it. Unresolved: t_haz_old (4212.00, 2026-01-29) has no refund credit. Skip: flood credit 1415.89 (the room absorbs the whole unearned premium).
 E4 hazard refund -> hazard projection, ACTION, affirmative: "The kept amount of a returned hazard premium is worked out only after the annual hazard premium on file has been reviewed against every hazard insurance bill received since it was last set." Skip: 2383.95.
 E5 hazard refund -> flood projection, ACTION: "The kept amount of a returned hazard premium is worked out only after the annual flood premium on file has been reviewed against every flood insurance bill received since it was last set." Skip: 2498.92.
 Four-point test: each sentence joins its own result with an ordering connective (not ... until / only after), waits on a named review (action) or a record-visible credit (state), names no tool/id/code token, hard strength, exact scope. Directions: hazard-refund rule affirmative, flood-refund rule negated for reviews and affirmative for the credit; the tax rule (task 0) negated - the charter carries both. Owner=user problems: both returned premiums (the executor moves estate money; synchronous; receipts in the transcript). Topological order: hazard review, flood review (commute: different fields, neither reads the other), hazard refund, flood refund. user_scenario mentions none of the prerequisites (homeowners refund only on the agent's question; reviews only as passive consent).

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. setaside_charges_updated <- setaside_charge_review: update_from_bill satisfied by the replacement installment bills (q_haz_2, q_fl_2, on file for this reserve). Overwrites declared on the separate clauses "the annual hazard premium is the billed_amount of the current hazard policy term" and "the annual flood premium is the billed_amount of the current flood policy term". setaside_refund_credit <- setaside_evt_refund: refund_active (reserve active), refund_once (t_haz_old / t_fl_old not yet refunded; credits 2793.61 <= 4212.00 and 1406.46 <= 1750.00). Overwrite of "the refunded amount is credited back to the set-aside per refund_credit_target" scoped to returned hazard / flood premiums; each tail names the two sibling cases and leaves every other refund under base. No time gates.

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Reserve of loan 7258314097 (customer Walter Hargrove; caller Ellen Hargrove, successor). Hazard: withdrawn term bill q_haz_old (2026-03-01, 4212.00) paid by t_haz_old; replacement HO3 policy AS-HO3-118204 billed in two installments q_haz_1 (due 2026-06-01, paid 2026-04-28 by t_haz_1) and q_haz_2 (due 2026-12-01, received). Flood: withdrawn NFIP term q_fl_old (2026-04-15, 1750.00) paid by t_fl_old; private policy PFX-22-480613 installments q_fl_1 (due 2026-06-15, paid 2026-05-12 by t_fl_1), q_fl_2 (due 2026-12-15, received). Tax: q_tax / t_tax (2025 bill, 7594.00) - read as it stands. Credits correlate to t_haz_old and t_fl_old by source_txn_ref.

6. FACTOR CARD (tier taken / figure with that factor at its default, round-3 structure).
 Structure after round 3 (renderer finding, assembly class): each projection's computation document defines every assembled quantity with its default - current premium (latest paid bill), renewal premium (current premium increased once by the renewal loading = standard renewal increase 4 percent plus the premium-change, occupancy/residence and appraisal loadings, each zero by default), pay-plan fee (zero by default, hazard), renewal share (one half by default) and the blend, stated once. Each factor document only replaces its own quantity, and with every other factor at its default each factor moves the result on its own (solo runs from the all-default figures: hazard 2876.40 -> hu_plan 5752.80, hu_change 2989.20, hu_occ 3017.40, hu_appraisal 2961.00, hu_fee 2888.40, hu_span 2857.60; flood 1473.90 -> fu_plan 2947.80, fu_change 1531.70, fu_residence 1618.40, fu_appraisal 1517.25, fu_span 1459.45).
 Hazard projection: hu_plan M pay-plan basis 2820+2820=5640 / 3095.20; hu_change P high 8% (5640 > 4212 x 1.10: the borrower's own switch in June at 2026 coastal rates, both terms occupied-rated) / 6028.00; hu_occ P vacant-home 10% (profile closed + death case D&P; multi-source) / 5990.40 - premise holds: the current term was written 2026-06-01 while the borrower lived there and renews 2027-06-01 on an empty house; hu_appraisal P high 6% (case appraisal 1185000 of 2026-07-28 > 1050000 x 1.10; maturity + jumbo) / 6065.60; hu_fee P semiannual 12.00 (two bills) / 6166.40; hu_span M replacement month basis 4/12 (default one half) / 6441.60. Result 6178.40 (5640 x 8/12 + 7219.20 x 4/12 + 12, renewal loading 4+8+10+6 = 28 percent applied once); all-default 2876.40.
 Flood projection: fu_plan M 2890.00 / 1582.28; fu_change P 8% (2890 > 1750 x 1.10) / 3106.75; fu_residence P estate residence 20% / 3020.05 - premise holds: the private term was written 2026-06-15 for the borrower's primary residence and is rated as a non-primary residence at its 2027-06-15 renewal; fu_appraisal P 6% / 3121.20; fu_span M 3/12 (default one half) / 3439.10. Result 3164.55 (2890 x 9/12 + 3988.20 x 3/12, loading 4+8+20+6 = 38); all-default 1473.90.
 Returned hazard premium (default 3150.35 = by days, no release): hr_basis M short-rate (92 days, months in force 3, cancellation date = paid replacement bill due 2026-06-01) 4212 x 8/12 = 2808.00 / 2964.79; hr_horizon M deadline 2027-01-06 -> 2 months / 2808.00; hr_insneed M quarter blocks (two hazard payments in 12 months) / 2404.33; hr_cushion P estate cushion 2 months (closed profile + death case; multi-source, cross-difficulty residency) / 1404.00; hr_floor P leaving-home 0.00 (intent sell_property) / 2808.00 (excess 28.77 below the 50.00 standard floor); hr_retain P half (inspection fee 2025-12-10, no corporate advance) / 2779.23. Result 2793.61.
 Returned flood premium (default 1457.53): fr_basis M duplicate coverage ((1750-50) x 304/365 = 1415.89) / 1427.28; fr_horizon M 2 months / 1415.89; fr_insneed M quarter blocks / 1017.17; fr_cushion P estate cushion 3 months / 707.95; fr_floor P 0.00 / 1415.89 (excess 18.86); fr_retain P half / 1397.03. Result 1406.46.
 Refund policies checked for the assembly class: their computation documents already define every assembled quantity with its default (tax part, insurance part, cushion zero, room, excess, standard release floor, the borrower keeping the whole released excess) and state the assembly once; every factor replaces only a quantity that document defines. The floor and the retention share act on the excess, which is a quantity of the computation document, not of another factor; whether an excess exists is a fact of the world, and on each task world every refund factor moves the result (sensitivity above). No change made there.
 Method pairwise inputs: plan bases differ by sum vs single bill vs on-file figure; span bases by months-since-replacement vs paid/received count vs one half; hazard basis flat = whole payment, short-rate = whole months after the cancellation month, by days = (365 - days)/365 (92 days: 2808.00 vs 3150.35); flood basis fee-first proration vs plain proration vs whole; horizon deadline vs good-through vs period left (2 vs 6 here); insneed renewal-date vs quarter blocks vs prorated.
 Double-loading check (round 2 class sweep, still holds): hu_occ / fu_residence price the move from occupied to unoccupied / non-primary rating at renewal on terms written before the death; hu_change / fu_change price premium momentum between two occupied-rated terms; hu_appraisal prices coverage keeping pace with value; hu_fee is the pay-plan charge; the standard renewal increase is the default trend every renewal carries. Nothing is charged twice.
 Factor independence: every factor's tier reads only its own evidence bindings; renewal_prem, tax_part, ins_part, need, room, excess, released and result are plain assembly. Whole-input floors: history zeroed and cross-category forced off each change every result (check_compute).

7. SEED. customers Walter (borrower, deceased) and Ellen (successor_in_interest linked to Walter). jumbo_loans Summit Fixed Lump Sum, SC, closing 2025-04-08, funded 2025-04-12, due and payable 2026-07-06, principal 567960.92 = opening 495000.00 + reserve advance postings + inspection fee 24.00 + 18 monthly accruals at 6.95% on month-end balances. Reserve: 21466.00 funded = 24 months of the closing charges (tax 6455.00 + hazard 2795.00 + flood 1483.00) x 2; payments 2025-12-29 tax 7594.00, 2026-01-29 hazard 4212.00, 2026-03-13 NFIP 1750.00 (+18% glide from 1483.00), 2026-04-28 hazard installment 2820.00, 2026-05-12 flood installment 1445.00; balance 3645.00. Residency: Standard Annual Certification, inspection 2025-12-10 (vacancy report while he was in hospital; fee 24.00 posted to the Summit ledger) found him in occupancy; certified 2026-03-30; profile closed 2026-06-20 on his death. Maturity: Death of Last Surviving Borrower, opened and called due 2026-07-06 (no HUD step on Summit), response 2026-08-05, resolution 2027-01-06, appraisal 2026-07-28 1185000.00, successor Ellen, intent sell_property. Automatic clauses: no growth; payments continue while due and payable; the received second installments fall due 2026-12-01 / 2026-12-15 (30-day lead ends 2026-11-01 / 2026-11-15 - not owed at frozen_time); no depletion; no notice tool.

8. PERSONA. Brisk executor. Volunteered (entailed): father's death on June 20, successor status, house being sold, the NFIP policy he cancelled in June for a private policy with higher limits (q_fl_old withdrawn, q_fl_1 from 2026-06-15), the refund check of 1415.89 deposited in the estate account (= the duplicate-coverage unearned figure = fr_horizon / fr_floor baseline, not gold). On request: name/phone, DOB/ZIP, SSN last four, loan number. Only on the agent's question: the homeowners refund of 2808.00 (= short-rate unearned, not gold) for the policy he replaced on June 1, deposited in July. Passive: consent to reviews; accepts partial keeping; runs each payment with the amount and references read to her; closes when credited.

9. REACHABILITY. Identity (name+phone, DOB+ZIP) -> loan via her linked borrower id -> reserve, bills, ledger, occupancy profile + events, death case, Summit ledger. The flood refund rule sends the agent to both reviews and to the hazard credit; the agent asks about other insurer refunds (she confirms 2808.00), posts both reviews, works out 2793.61 and hands over the hazard payment, then 1406.46 and hands over the flood payment. One frozen_time, nothing awaited.

10. GT. Steps 0-9 reads; 10/11 hazard review (q_haz_2, 6178.40); 12/13 flood review (q_fl_2, 3164.55); 14/15 hazard payment (t_haz_old, 2793.61, owner user); 16/17 flood payment (t_fl_old, 1406.46, owner user). Terminal: hazard 6178.40, flood 3164.55 on file; two refund credits; balance 3645.00 + 2793.61 + 1406.46 = 7845.07.

11. RUNS (round 3). Scratch evaluator: projections 6178.40 / 3164.55, refunds 2793.61 / 1406.46, every factor biting (figures above); skip runs as in section 3. Gates --task 1 and full block re-run green (see final report).

12. EDGE PROBES (round-3 world, scratch copies; hazard proj / flood proj / hazard credit / flood credit): gold 6178.40 / 3164.55 / 2793.61 / 1406.46. Resolved older maturity case on the same loan -> unchanged (status filters). No maturity case -> horizon 6, cushion 0, floor 50, loadings drop: 5877.60 / 2976.70 / 2808.00 / 1415.89. Withdrawn payoff case -> unchanged. No occupancy profile, or a profile still current -> 5990.40 / 3020.05 / 1404.00 / 707.95 (no vacancy or residence loading, no cushion). No inspection fee -> 2779.23 / 1411.41. Older unpaid withdrawn hazard bill (2025 term) -> unchanged (the latest withdrawn bill is selected). Old hazard bill not withdrawn -> the projection counts it as an installment (11177.60, installment-count share 2/3) and there is no withdrawn term to credit (0.00), as the rules state. No paid replacement -> carry-forward basis with the default share one half (4633.20) and the by-days refund on the handling date (1592.48). No bills -> projections carry the figures on file at the default share, refunds 0. Renewal share runs: replacement month 4/12 (gold), installment count when nothing is withdrawn, default one half otherwise. No raise, no zero division.

13. REVISIONS. Round 1: (a) moved-out cushion tier rewritten to "an occupancy inspection was ordered on it within the twelve months"; (b) projection rules pin the bill relied on; (c) tax 7594.00 chosen to avoid half-cent ties.
 Round 2 (audit F-T1-1 SOURCE-FACTOR RED: vacancy loadings charged on replacement terms already bought for the empty house). Root cause: the seed made the current hazard and flood terms post-death vacant-house / empty-house replacements, contradicting the stated premise of hu_occ ("renews at unoccupied rates") and fu_residence ("rated as a non-primary residence at the next renewal"), and hu_change / fu_change then measured the vacancy repricing again. Fix at the seed (the factors are a legitimate schedule): the replacements are now the borrower's own switches made before his death on the occupied house (HO3 AS-HO3-118204 from 2026-06-01, private flood PFX-22-480613 with higher limits from 2026-06-15), so the loadings price the coming renewal repricing exactly once; NFIP 2026 premium 1750.00 (+18% from 1483.00), closing charges 6431.40 / 2795.00 / 1483.00, refund checks 2808.00 / 1415.89; persona lines rewritten. All four scored writes changed (round-2 values 6103.20 / 3135.65 / 2795.53 / 1403.08); every factor still bites; excesses 24.95 / 25.63 stay under the 50.00 standard floor, no half-cent ties. Audit O-4 closed: the flood rule's state sentence now says "the latest withdrawn hazard insurance term" (rule, policy_source, condition, closure). Propagated: initial_state, user_scenario, gold arguments, objectives/necessity, computations (factor_trace, factor_sensitivity, baseline_result), prerequisite_closure (edges, unresolved evidence, skip effects, order note), solvability_contract (business effects, user inputs, seed checks), argument tracing, this worklog.

 Round 3 (renderer, assembly class in the projection policies): the computation documents of the hazard and flood projections now define every assembled quantity with its default - current premium, renewal premium with the renewal loading = standard renewal increase 4 percent plus the premium-change, occupancy/residence and appraisal loadings (each zero by default), pay-plan fee zero (hazard), renewal share one half - and state the blend once; each factor document replaces only its own quantity, so each factor moves the result on its own (solo runs in section 6). Scored values changed: hazard 6103.20 -> 6178.40, flood 3135.65 -> 3164.55; to keep the release-floor and retention tiers biting the closing tax figure was recalibrated 6431.40 -> 6455.00 (initial reserve 21466.00, balance 3645.00), giving hazard credit 2793.61 (excess 28.77) and flood credit 1406.46 (excess 18.86), no half-cent ties. Refund policies checked for the class (section 6): already conforming, unchanged. Propagated: initial_state (reserve figures, opening funding), gold arguments, reserve-read objective, computations, prerequisite_closure (flip texts, skip effects 2383.95 / 1119.69, 2498.92 / 1200.17, 1415.89), solvability_contract (business effects, seed checks), argument tracing, this worklog; probes re-run (section 12).

14. DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT: request -> flood refund rule -> its three sentences send the agent to the two reviews (replacement bills received after the figures) and to the unrefunded latest withdrawn hazard payment -> hazard refund rule (also waiting on both reviews) -> same objects (q_haz_2, q_fl_2, t_haz_old, t_fl_old), same order, same figures as gold.
user_scenario:
You are Ellen Hargrove, fifty-eight, a hospital billing supervisor in Charleston and the daughter and executor of Walter Hargrove, who died on June 20 of this year. Cedarline already has you on file as the successor on your father's Cedarline Summit reverse mortgage, and you are getting his house on Harbor View Road on James Island ready to sell. You are brisk and organised, you keep a folder for every estate letter, and you like to finish one thing at a time.

You are calling because this week a refund check arrived from your father's old flood insurance, the federal flood program policy he cancelled in June, a few days before he died, when he moved to a private flood policy with higher limits; the check is made out to him and you have deposited it in the estate's account, and it is for $1,415.89. You understand that Cedarline paid that flood premium out of the tax and insurance reserve on the loan, so you want to pay the refund back into the reserve today, by phone, from the estate's checking account. You open with exactly that: you have a refund from your father's old flood insurance and you want to put it back into the loan's tax and insurance reserve.

When the agent asks who is calling, you give your name, Ellen Hargrove, your phone number, 4155520742, and you explain you are calling about your father Walter Hargrove's loan. Only when the agent asks for more to confirm who you are do you give your date of birth, 1968-08-30, and the ZIP code of your father's house, 29412; if asked for the last four of your own Social Security number you give 2386. If the agent asks for the loan number, you read 7258314097 from his statement. You do not know how the reserve works, how much is in it, or what insurance figures Cedarline keeps on file, and you say so if asked.

Only if the agent asks whether any other insurer has sent the estate money do you mention that in July the old homeowners insurance company also sent a refund check for $2,808.00 for the policy your father replaced on June 1, that you deposited it in the estate account, and that you are happy to pay that back as well if the agent says it belongs in the reserve. If the agent tells you that figures on the reserve have to be reviewed first, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent explains that the reserve only keeps part of a refund and the estate keeps the rest, you accept that and ask for each figure to be repeated so you can note it for the estate accounts. Whenever the agent hands a payment over to you to make yourself, you make it for exactly the amount and references the agent reads out, and you read back the confirmation. Once you hear that the money you sent has been credited to the reserve, you thank the agent and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two premium reviews (steps 11 and 13) write different fields of the reserve and neither computation reads the other's output, so either order gives the same terminal state and the same figures (verified: the hazard projection reads only hazard bills, occupancy, maturity and closing appraisal; the flood projection only flood bills and the same cross records). The two refund credits share the reserve balance and room; their order is pinned by the flood rule's own sentence 'The kept amount of a returned flood premium is fixed only after the reserve's payment of the latest withdrawn hazard insurance term carries a refund credit.', and both refund rules wait on both premium reviews ('...is worked out only after the annual hazard/flood premium on file has been reviewed...', '...is not settled until...'), so the only admissible orders are the two reviews in either order, then the hazard credit, then the flood credit.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the flood review leaves 1750.00 on file: the returned hazard premium credit becomes 2498.92 and the returned flood premium 1200.17 instead of 2793.61 and 1406.46; annual_flood_premium stays 1750.00.
Skipping the hazard review leaves 4212.00 on file: the credits become 2383.95 and 1119.69 instead of 2793.61 and 1406.46; annual_hazard_premium stays 4212.00.

Without the hazard credit the balance stays 3645.0, the flood room is larger, no excess remains and the returned flood premium credit is 1415.89 instead of 1406.46; the hazard refund credit row is also missing.
With 4212.00 still on file the hazard credit is 2383.95 instead of 2793.61.
With 1750.00 still on file the hazard credit is 2498.92 instead of 2793.61.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The opening asks only to pay the old flood insurance refund back into the reserve. The persona never mentions Cedarline's premium figures, a review, or the homeowners refund on her own; the homeowners refund check is disclosed only 'if the agent asks whether any other insurer has sent the estate money', and the review appears only as a passive consent ('If the agent tells you that figures on the reserve have to be reviewed first, you tell them to go ahead').
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Each refund tool writes the credit and the new balance whatever the premiums on file or other credits are; each update tool writes any figure passed. No tool reads another problem's state or refuses (task_tools.py function bodies).
